cards.title: Pakistan's mango exports fall 36pc amid US-Iran war: exporters' association
cards.author: Anadolu Agency
cards.why: This illustrates the tangible impact of regional geopolitical conflicts on Pakistan’s agricultural exports and foreign exchange earnings.
cards.summary: Pakistan's mango exports dropped 36 percent this year to 78,000 tonnes, down from 123,000 tonnes last year. The All Pakistan Fruit and Vegetables Exporters Association attributes this decline to the US-Iran war, which caused a sharp rise in freight costs and disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz. Middle Eastern countries, a primary market for Pakistani mangoes, saw the steepest reduction in imports.
key_facts: Mango exports fell by 36 percent this year.
Total exports dropped from 123,000 tonnes last year to 78,000 tonnes this year.
Freight rates surged from $1,000–$1,400 to $8,000 due to the US-Iran conflict.
Export earnings from mangoes declined from approximately $100 million to $60 million.
Pakistan historically ranked sixth in global mango production.

vocab.meaning: Likely to decay or go bad quickly.
A vital waterway between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

text: Pakistan’s mango exports fell 36 per cent this year as the US-Iran war disrupted shipping routes and drove up freight costs, industry figures showed on Wednesday.
According to All Pakistan Fruit and Vegetables Exporters Association, the country exported 78,000 tonnes of mangoes this year, compared with 123,000 tons last year.
Exports to the Middle East, a major market for Pakistani mangoes, dropped from 36,000 tonnes last year to 14,500 tonnes this year, the association said.
Waheed Ahmed, head of the association, told Anadolu that the ongoing conflict had reduced the country’s mango export earnings from approximately $100 million to around $60m.
He cited the months-long near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route, and rising freight rates as major factors behind the decline, particularly in exports to Middle Eastern countries.

“The freight rate that was $1,000-1,400 before the US-Iran war, now stands at $8,000. Secondly, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz also increased the shipping period , which affected the exports of perishable items like mangoes,” he said.
Ahmed said the United Arab Emirates and Oman were the main Middle Eastern destinations for Pakistani mangoes, particularly the internationally acclaimed Chaunsa variety, followed by Saudi Arabia.
Kuwait and Qatar also import significant quantities of Pakistani mangoes, according to the association.
Mango exports to neighboring Afghanistan were also disrupted by frequent border closures amid strained relations between the two countries, Ahmed said.
Pakistan produced 1.9m metric tonnes of mangoes annually until 2018, ranking sixth globally behind India, China, Thailand, Indonesia and Mexico.
However, production has declined over the past four years, with the association attributing the drop to global warming.
Climate change has reduced Pakistan’s total mango production by 35pc, according to the association.

cards.title: ICJ report sees 'judicial capture' in Pakistan after 26th, 27th Constitutional Amendments
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: It provides an international legal perspective on significant constitutional changes that impact the separation of powers and judicial independence in Pakistan.
cards.summary: The International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) reports that the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments have resulted in systemic judicial capture in Pakistan. By establishing the Federal Constitutional Court and altering the Judicial Commission of Pakistan, the government has eroded the independence of the higher judiciary. The report concludes that these reforms deviate from the judicial independence standards established following the 2009 movement.
key_facts: The 26th Amendment was passed in October 2024.
The 27th Amendment established the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC).
The ICJ report is titled 'Judicial Capture: Independence of the Judiciary in Pakistan after the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments'.
Two Supreme Court judges resigned in protest following the 27th Amendment.

vocab.meaning: A form of political corruption where the judiciary is manipulated by other branches of government.
Done or shown openly; not secret.

text: A report released by the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) on Wednesday said that the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments led to a “systemic judicial capture” in Pakistan.

The 26th Amendment , passed in October 2024, carved constitutional benches out of the Supreme Court, with their members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) in which judges no longer held a majority.

Barely a year later, the 27th Amendment turned those benches into an entirely separate court, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC). It also made significant changes to the judicial system, the military’s chain of command and granted immunities to government officials. Two of the SC’s senior-most judges resigned in protest the day it became law.
On Wednesday, the ICJ released a report — titled ‘ Judicial Capture: Independence of the Judiciary in Pakistan after the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments ’.

It said that after analysing the institutional framework governing higher courts following the two amendments, the judiciary in Pakistan no longer enjoyed institutional guarantees of independence required under international law and standards.
“The 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments were a decisive break from the model of judicial independence that Pakistan had built after the restoration of the judiciary in 2009,” the report noted.
However, it observed that the “erosion of judicial independence” was done through constitutional amendments, rather than the overt removal of judges.

The report said that while the government argued that amendments were made to “check judicial overreach, reduce the backlog of cases, end the perceived politicisation of the SC’s original jurisdiction and give Parliament a role in judicial appointments comparable to that of legislatures in other democracies”, the claims did not justify “changing the judicial structure in a manner that is glaringly inconsistent with Pakistan’s obligations under international law”.

It also acknowledged that the Supreme Court had “encroached into roles of Parliament and other institutions”. However, it also noted that with the 26th and 27th amendments, the Parliament failed to ensure these “deficiencies” were fixed in line with judicial independence.
“Instead, the 26th and 27th Amendments have led to systemic judicial capture by other branches of the state and the dismantling of the rule of law in the country,” the ICJ stated.
It was found that the ruling coalition had “exploited” the public’s grievances over the functioning of courts in a “self-serving manner” to control the judiciary.

“As a result, even the highest courts of the land in Pakistan no longer serve as a check on the executive or the Parliament and their function as avenues for redress of victims of human rights violations is seriously impaired,” the report stated.
Call for comprehensive review

In its recommendations, the report appealed to the government to begin a comprehensive review of the amendments and their implementation in “light of international law and standards”, particularly under the framework of Pakistan’s obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) and by holding “transparent and broad” public consultation.

It suggested that the government engage in international cooperation, including seeking technical assistance from the UN special rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers and inviting them for a country visit.
In its recommendations to the JCP, the ICJ called on it to revise the criteria for judicial appointments in accordance with international law, standards and best practices.
It further suggested: “Ensure the published criteria are the sole basis for nomination of judges to the FCC, the SC, the high courts and constitutional benches of the high courts.”

It also called on the commission to establish a transparent procedure for appointments and publish reasons for each appointment that “demonstrate the published criteria are being implemented in practice”.
It also called on the JCP to refrain from transferring a high court judge without their consent.

In its recommendations to the Supreme Judicial Council, the ICJ said: “Define ‘inefficiency’ in a manner that is consistent with international standards to only mean serious incompetence that renders judges unfit to discharge their duties.”

For the Special Parliamentary Committee , which has the power to nominate the chief justice of Pakistan, the report called for it to adopt “clear and transparent criteria and procedures” for the appointment of the SC and FCC top judges and to publish the reasons for each selection.

Lastly, the report urged the FCC, the SC and the high courts to “interpret and apply the provisions of the 26th and 27th Amendments, to the greatest extent possible, in a manner consistent with the independence of the judiciary as guaranteed by Article 14 of the ICCPR”.

cards.title: Pakistan conducts successful launch of Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile: ISPR
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: Military advancements and deterrence capabilities are standard topics for Pakistan Affairs and national security discussions.
cards.summary: The Pakistan Army successfully tested the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, enhancing its strategic defense and operational flexibility. The missile features advanced navigation and propulsion systems capable of high-precision strikes at long ranges. The development is described as a milestone for the Army Rocket Force Command and national deterrence.
key_facts: The Fatah-3 is a supersonic cruise missile.
The test was conducted by the Pakistan Army.
The missile is equipped with advanced navigation and propulsion systems.
It is designed to enhance the operational flexibility of the Army Rocket Force Command.

vocab.meaning: The action of discouraging an action or event through instilling doubt or fear of the consequences.
Involving or denoting a speed greater than that of sound.

text: The Pakistan Army on Wednesday successfully launched the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, according to the military’s media wing.

In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said, “The Pakistan Army successfully conducted the launch of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, marking another significant milestone in strengthening Pakistan’s national defence capabilities.
“The weapon system is equipped with advanced navigation and propulsion systems and is capable of engaging targets at long range with high precision and lethality at supersonic speed,” it said.

It added that the missile would “significantly enhance the operational flexibility and strike range of the Pakistan Army’s Rocket Force Command, further strengthening the country’s overall conventional deterrence and defence posture”.
According to the statement, the Army Rocket Force Command commander, senior officers from the armed forces, scientists and engineers witnessed the launch.

It added that President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, and the services chiefs congratulated the team on the successful launch.
They appreciated the dedication and commitment of all personnel involved in achieving this significant milestone in Pakistan’s defence development, the statement concluded.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar termed the development a “testament to the relentless hard work, skill and innovation of our teams in strengthening Pakistan’s defence capabilities and national deterrence”.
“The entire nation takes immense pride in their unwavering commitment to keeping the country strong and secure,” he said.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the successful launch. According to the interior ministry, he said that the launch represented a “significant advancement in the defence sector”.
“The successful test of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile marks a major milestone in the country’s defence capabilities,” Naqvi said.
Earlier this month, the Pakistan Air Force performed a successful flight test of the country’s first indigenously developed air-to-air missile, Fa’az.
ISPR said that the flight test marked “another significant milestone in the advancement of national aerospace and defence capabilities”.

In October, Pakistan successfully tested two missiles; the Fatah-2 extended-range hypersonic ballistic missile was tested on Oct 13 and the indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile was tested on Oct 6.

cards.title: Asean secretary general to undertake working visit to Pakistan from Nov 18-20
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: It highlights Pakistan's efforts to diversify its foreign policy and deepen engagement with the Southeast Asian bloc.
cards.summary: ASEAN Secretary General Dr. Kao Kim Hourn is visiting Pakistan from November 18 to 20 to strengthen diplomatic and economic ties. This marks the first high-level visit from the ASEAN Secretariat in over two decades. The visit aims to review regional cooperation, trade, and investment opportunities.
key_facts: Dr. Kao Kim Hourn is the Secretary General of ASEAN.
Pakistan has been an ASEAN Sectoral Dialogue Partner since 1993.
Pakistan became a member of the ASEAN Regional Forum in 2004.
This is the first high-level visit from the ASEAN Secretariat to Pakistan in over 20 years.

vocab.meaning: The office or department of a secretary; the administrative body of an organization.
Relating to a particular sector or branch of activity.
